description: Maps error patterns to common mistakes and fixes checked against the current teaching reference

patterns.title: Null-Check Ordering (CRITICAL)
patterns.description: Checking array/string length without null check first causes NullReferenceException instead of ContractViolationException.
patterns.wrongExample: requires arr.Length > 0        // Crashes if arr is null!
patterns.correctExample:
requires arr != null       // First: reject null
requires arr.Length > 0    // Then: check length
patterns.explanation: Contracts are evaluated in order. Reading arr.Length when arr is null throws instead of reporting the intended contract violation. Guard reference types with x != null before accessing their properties.

patterns.title: String Operation Syntax
patterns.description: Use ordinary .NET string members and preserve their argument counts.
patterns.wrongExample: return type + ":" + id         // id is an int: convert it explicitly with id.ToString()
patterns.explanation: Use ToString(), +, string.Format() and Length. Calor strings interpolate ${expression}; escape literal format placeholders as \${0}.

patterns.title: Variable Redeclaration
patterns.description: Declare a variable once. Use var for a mutable binding and set for later updates.
patterns.wrongExample:
let k = rng % n    // First use: declares k
let k = k + 1      // ERROR - 'k' already defined
patterns.correctExample:
var k = rng % n
set k k + 1
patterns.explanation: let and var declare bindings. A second declaration with the same name is not an update. Use set name expression to update a mutable binding.

patterns.title: Character Literal Syntax
patterns.description: A single-quoted character literal must contain one UTF-16 code unit or a valid C# escape sequence.
patterns.correctExample:
let char:digit = '0'
let char:newline = '\n'
let int:offset = c - '0'
patterns.explanation: Use single quotes for char and double quotes for string. Escapes such as '\n', '\\', '\'', and '\u0041' represent one character. Empty literals, multiple characters, raw line breaks, and invalid escapes are rejected.

patterns.title: Array Type Syntax
patterns.description: Array types use C# suffix brackets: int[], string[] or int[,].
patterns.wrongExample: func UseItems ([int:items) → int     // ERROR - array brackets go after the type
patterns.correctExample:
func UseItems (int[]:items) → int
  return items.Length
func UseOtherItems (int[]:items) → int
  return items.Length
patterns.explanation: Keep array brackets balanced and retain the element type and rank. Prefix arrays such as [int] and aliases such as i32 are retired.

patterns.title: Array Element Access
patterns.description: Use bracket indexing in expressions and set for element updates.
patterns.wrongExample: let x = arr.get(i)     // ERROR - arrays have no get method; index with arr[i]
patterns.correctExample:
let x = arr[i]
set arr[i] value

var sum = 0
set sum sum + data[i]
patterns.explanation: arr[i] is an expression and can appear inside operators and contracts. A temporary binding is optional. Element updates must declare the appropriate mutation effect.

patterns.title: String Comparison
patterns.description: Relational operators (< >) do not order strings. Use equality or an explicit .NET comparison.
patterns.wrongExample:
if a < b               // ERROR - can't compare strings with <
  return -1
patterns.explanation: Use == for equality. For ordinal ordering use string.Compare with StringComparison.Ordinal; use an explicit culture when culture-sensitive ordering is intended.

patterns.title: Missing Built-in Operators
patterns.description: Bare abs, max, min, sqrt and pow names are not built-in operators. Use ordinary Math methods or explicit branches.
patterns.wrongExample:
return abs(x)     // ERROR - abs doesn't exist
return max(a, b)  // ERROR - max doesn't exist
patterns.explanation: Use Math.Abs, Math.Max, Math.Min, Math.Sqrt or Math.Pow with compatible argument types. Ordinary .NET overflow and domain behavior still applies.

patterns.title: Integer Literal Overflow
patterns.description: Retain the integer value and its C# width. Use an L suffix for long literals when needed.
patterns.wrongExample: let int:big = 1000000000000   // ERROR - too large for int
patterns.explanation: If a large positive source value became negative, inspect the original literal and conversion diagnostics. Do not repair overflow by guessing a replacement value.

patterns.title: Generic Type Parameters in Expressions
patterns.description: Use ordinary angle-bracket generic arguments in types and method calls. Keep required type arguments.
patterns.wrongExample: let info = EnumCache.GetInfo<T>   // ERROR - missing call parentheses
patterns.explanation: Preserve the resolved generic receiver and method type arguments; removing arguments can change overload resolution. For unsupported contexts, use calor convert and retain its converter-owned fallback; do not handwrite passthrough.

patterns.title: Expected Keyword
patterns.description: The parser expected a native Calor keyword or a correctly formed declaration.
patterns.wrongExample:
module MyApp
  function Add(a b)    // Use func and typed parameters
patterns.correctExample:
module MyApp
  func Add (int:a, int:b) → int
    return a + b
patterns.explanation: Use module Name and func Name (type:name, ...) → ReturnType. Section markers and the ASCII signature arrow are retired.

patterns.title: Invalid Modifier
patterns.description: A modifier keyword was used in an invalid position or an unrecognized modifier was applied to a declaration.
patterns.wrongExample: static func Helper () → int    // C# modifier before the Calor keyword
patterns.correctExample:
func Helper () → int
  return 0
func Good private () → int
  return 1
patterns.explanation: Visibility and modifiers follow the declaration name, before parameters: func Good private (...) → int. Use full spellings such as public, private and virtual; public is the default.

patterns.title: Type Parameter Not Found
patterns.description: A reference to a generic type parameter (like T, K, V) was used but the parameter is not declared in the current scope.
patterns.wrongExample: func Identity (T:x) → T      // T not declared as type param
patterns.explanation: Generic type parameters must be declared in the function or type name field using angle brackets. Ensure the type parameter name matches exactly (case-sensitive).

patterns.title: Invalid Reference
patterns.description: A reference to a variable, function, or type is invalid in the current context. This may be a scope issue or an attempt to use a binding before it is defined.
patterns.wrongExample: return a + b      // 'a' or 'b' not accessible in this scope
patterns.correctExample:
let a = 1
let b = 2
return a + b
patterns.explanation: Ensure the referenced name is defined and accessible in the current scope. Local let/var bindings are visible after their declaration point and within the same block.

patterns.title: Missing Extension Self Parameter
patterns.description: An extension function must declare its receiver as the first parameter with the this modifier.
patterns.correctExample:
func ToUpper (this string:self) → string
  return self.ToUpper()
patterns.explanation: Use this Type:name as the first parameter in a named static module. The receiver name need not be self. Preserve its type and extension-method identity.
